title: Compute Shadowing and Tenant Fairness Playbook (PRD)
body:
Summary:
This PRD proposes a feature set called "Compute Shadowing" paired with a Tenant Fairness Playbook to reduce noisy-neighbor incidents in Dedicated pools while preserving burst flexibility for paying customers. The idea is to provide lightweight, low-cost shadow resources and visibility hooks that (a) give product and platform teams an early signal of tenant-induced tail-latency, (b) enable controlled soft-bursting with bounded impact to co-tenants, and (c) expose transparent fairness metrics to customers so they can make tradeoffs (latency vs cost) proactively.

Problem / Motivation:
- We continue to see unpredictable tail latency in some dedicated pools during sudden tenant surges. Current mitigations (hard isolation by slabting, prewarming) are effective but either raise costs or reduce utilization.
- Customers want burst options but also predictable SLAs; platform teams need orchestration primitives that avoid "noisy neighbor" regressions without conservative overprovisioning.
- Lack of tenant-facing transparency leads to support churn: customers often only learn of contamination after failure.

Goals (what success looks like):
- Reduce incident rate due to cross-tenant interference by 50% in pilot pools within three months.
- Allow tenants to opt into one of three burst profiles (elastic, buffered, compensated) with clear cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Provide per-tenant fairness score and an "isolation exposure" metric surfaced in Console and via API.
- Keep incremental infra cost for shadowing under 8% of pool capacity (target).

Non-goals:
- This PRD does not replace hard-tenant siloing for customers who require strict physical isolation (those should still use isolated pools or Private).
- Not proposing an immediate rewrite of the serving runtime; integrate with existing autoscaler and router where possible.

High-level approach / Design pillars:
1) Shadowed Workloads: allocate a small, cost-constrained set of shadow slots per tenant that run sampled real requests in a lightweight, synthetic mode (shorter KV lifetime, quantized precision). Shadow workloads exercise contention points (memory, PCIe bandwidth, GPU SM activity) and produce contention signals without fully consuming tokens.
2) Fairness Scoring: compute a rolling fairness score per tenant based on observed resource contention, request tail latency delta vs baseline, and burst frequency. Scores normalized to 0..100 and exposed externally.
3) Soft-burst Modes: let tenants choose a burst profile with automated tradeoffs: 
   - Elastic: full burst when capacity exists; no guarantees; lowest cost.
   - Buffered: burst up to an assigned buffer; router enforces proportional shedding to protect fairness; small premium.
   - Compensated: burst accepted but usage is damped by transient throttles to maintain fairness; higher premium, preserves tail SLO.
4) Transparency & Negotiation API: surface isolation exposure and fairness score in Console with a simple action flow: increase buffer, buy compensated minutes, or request dedicated isolate. Also an API for programmatic negotiation.

Architecture / Components:
- Shadowing agent (lightweight probe) — runs inside runtime worker process; configurable sampling rate, execution mode (dry-run vs limited tokens), and metric emission.
- Fairness aggregator — time-series pipeline component that ingests per-worker signals (contention counters, tail-latency deltas) and computes per-tenant score and exposure index.
- Burst controller — policy layer that consumes fairness scores, tenant profile, and pool headroom to decide admission and proportionate shedding. Integrates with existing allocation broker.
- Console & API surface — Dashboard cards, tenant action panel, and REST endpoints.

Data model / Signals collected (examples):
- GPU SM occupancy spike trend (sampled windows)
- Memory bandwidth saturation counters (worker-local estimate)
- KV cache hit-rate deltas when other tenants increase concurrency
- Per-request p95/p99 delta compared to tenant baseline
- Shadow success-to-degradation ratio (how many sampled requests produced degraded outputs)

Autoscaler interactions:
- Autoscaler continues to manage pool scale using current policies. Shadow signals feed a parallel fast-path controller: when fairness score crosses a threshold, the Burst controller can request a small proactive scale-up (soft request) or temporarily limit buffer allocations.
- To avoid oscillation, the Shadow controller uses hold-down timers, hysteresis windows, and band-based decisions rather than immediate scale actions.

Burst options and billing model (proposal):
- Elastic: free within baseline quota; best-effort.
- Buffered: priced per-minute of buffer consumption; each tenant receives a small monthly buffer by default, top-ups billable.
- Compensated: billed at higher rate but provides a fairness-preserving throttle and guarantees on tail percentiles. Includes an SLA credit model if tail SLOs are missed due to platform faults.

Isolation controls (admin and customer-facing):
- Tenant-level "exposure threshold": admin setting that triggers automatic mitigations (reduce buffer, pause queued work) when crossed.
- "Temporary isolation voucher": for customers to buy a short window of stronger isolation (e.g., 30 minutes) routed to reserved slots for peak events.
- Platform-safe list: admins can mark tenants as "sensitive" preventing them from being scheduled in opportunistic nodes.

Console UX (mock flow):
- Pool view: new "Isolation Health" column with sparkline of exposure index.
- Tenant page: show Fairness Score, recent shadow test results, recommended actions (increase buffer / buy voucher / request dedicated slice).
- Incident view: when platform detects cross-tenant impact, auto-populate suggested runbook steps and correlate with recent shadow logs.

APIs: (sketch)
- GET /v1/tenants/{id}/fairness -> {score, exposure_index, last_sample}
- POST /v1/tenants/{id}/burst-request -> {profile: buffered|compensated|elastic, duration_minutes}
- GET /v1/pools/{id}/isolation-health -> timeseries
(Exact contract to be finalized with SDK team.)

Metrics / SLOs to track:
- Reduction in cross-tenant incident MTTR and frequency (target -50% incident frequency).
- Fraction of bursts that required emergency remediation.
- Average incremental infra cost for shadowing vs incident cost saved.
- Fairness score distribution across tenants (median, 90th)

Implementation plan (phases):
Phase 0 (experiment, 4 weeks): small pilot in one pool, shadow agent as feature flag. Collect baseline signals, iterate on heuristics.
Phase 1 (alpha, 8 weeks): implement fairness aggregator, basic Console card, expose API read endpoints. Pilot with two customers.
Phase 2 (beta, 12 weeks): implement buffered/compensated burst admission, billing hooks, admin controls, and rollout to 30% of dedicated pools.
Phase 3 (general release, 6 weeks): expand to all Dedicated pools, full billing integration, add isolation voucher product.

Risks and mitigations:
- False positives from probes: tune sampling and use ensemble heuristics combining latency and hardware counters.
- Cost of probes: limit shadow footprint and use quantized/summarized executions. Keep target <8% overhead.
- Customer confusion: emphasize clear Console language, defaults to elastic, and require explicit opt-in for compensated mode.

Operational runbooks (short):
- If pool exposure index spikes above 80: disable buffered admissions, enable temporary isolation vouchers, and alert on-call SRE.
- If repeated high exposure from one tenant: automatically flag for manual review, notify tenant owner with remediation suggestions.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How much pre-allocated buffer per tenant is reasonable by default? (pilot to determine).
- Do we allow cross-tenant market-like trading of buffer credits? (complexity vs potential revenue).
- Best way to surface fairness without creating regulatory or contractual issues around discrimination of workloads? Legal review required.

Rollout communication and customer-facing docs:
- Draft a short explainer for Console (what fairness score means) and a FAQ for common scenarios.
- Technical blog later showing how shadowing reduced incidents in pilot.

Appendix: quick simulation notes (team sheet)
- Run capacity sim with heavy-LLM tier and 1% of request sampling; synthetic tenant bursts at +6x baseline for 15 minutes. Measure p99 delta and GPU occupancy ratios.
- Link to initial simulation sheet: sheet:team-capacity-simulations-2025

Next steps (for this PRD):
- Align on scope with Runtime and SRE (tech feasibility review).
- Spin up pilot: assign a dev owner, SRE partner, and one customer for early alpha.
- Legal review for fairness scoring exposure and potential SLA language.

Authors / contacts:
- Product: Aisha Patel (owner), Lydia Nguyen
- Runtime: Marco Ruiz
- SRE: Omar Wallace
- UX: Sofie Berg

Note: this is a working doc — expect heuristics and names to change after the feasibility pass.
